body.statement: There are universal constants \(0<c<C<\infty\) such that, for every admissible degree sequence, \[\Pr\!\left\{c\,r(n,d_n)\le R(G_n)\le C\,r(n,d_n)\right\}\longrightarrow1.\] The upper inequality is attained by the one-shot graph-measurable design-estimator returned by the finite compiler, and the lower inequality ranges over every graph-dependent assignment distribution and measurable estimator. This strictly tightens KandirosHarshawSavje2026Minimax, Corollary 5.4, from the factor-\(d_n\) interval \(d_n/n\lesssim R(G_n)\lesssim d_n^2/n\) to a matched order, and strictly improves the KandirosEtAl2024ConflictGraph generic \(d_n^2/n\) GATE upper scale by the factor \(\log(d_n+1)\).
body.justification: This resolves the full two-arm, all-procedure minimax order rather than optimizing a fixed estimator or exposing only one endpoint arm.
body.gap: The closest published result is KandirosHarshawSavje2026Minimax, Corollary 5.4, whose bounds differ by a polynomial factor \(d_n\); the January 2026 one-arm talk is not a full-GATE theorem.
body.consumer: ShiEtAl2020FreedomChoice motivates sizing a larger all-free versus all-fixed random-regular public-goods experiment by the explicit precision cost \(d_n^2/\log(d_n+1)\).
